sense: reveal, bring to light: a plot, a fraud

terms.comment: Properly to throw open (a gate, a road); then to disclose a secret, expose a plot or a person: patefactus, found out, convicted (Cic. Cat. 3.15). Cicero pairs it with prōferre, bring forward (Mil. 103).
Properly to take the cover off, unroof (the wind took the roof off the farmhouse, Plaut. Rud. 1.1.3); then to reveal or detect a plot, a plan.

evidence: Cic. Fl. 11: vincī, refellī, coarguī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A word of the courts, most frequent in Cicero: to refute someone, prove him guilty.

phrases.latin: sī hoc cēlātur, in metū, sīn patefit, in probrō sum
phrases.english: if this is kept hidden, I live in fear; if it comes out, I’m disgraced

sources: Lewis & Short: patefacio · Lewis & Short: detego · Lewis & Short: coarguo
